hook.text: Socrates never gave answers. He asked questions that led people to discover the answers themselves. The method still.

buildup.text: Telling people what to think creates resistance. Leading them to the insight through questions creates ownership.

discovery.text: Ask questions like: 'What would happen if we tried X?' or 'What are we assuming that might not be true?'

twist.text: People defend ideas they discovered themselves. If your question led them there, they'll champion it willingly.

climax.text: Replace your next three statements in meetings with questions. Watch how the dynamic shifts toward collaboration.

punchline.text: Ask, don't tell. Let them own the insight.

quiz.question: Why is asking questions more influential than giving answers?
options: Questions take less preparation than statements
People champion ideas they discover themselves through guided questioning
Questions make the asker appear more intelligent
